# EvoScientist v0.3.5 — GPT-6.1 Sol, `EvoSci setup` & Profile Memory That Survives Growth

G'Day! v0.3.5 adds **GPT-6.1 Sol** on OpenAI and OpenRouter and introduces **`EvoSci setup`**, the first piece of the new installer: it brings in **Node.js** for the WebUI and `npx` MCP servers, and gives the agent's shell a **research Python with numpy, pandas, matplotlib and scipy** when the machine has no usable `python`. It also fixes **profile memory vanishing from the prompt** once the profile files grow past their budget. Under the hood: deepagents 0.7.21 and a routine dependency refresh (anthropic SDK 1.11, openai SDK 3.24, langchain-core 1.6.6).

---

### 🔌 Models (#553)
- **GPT-6.1 Sol** — `gpt-6.1-sol` (OpenAI) and `openai/gpt-6.1-sol` (OpenRouter), with the 1.05M context window and reasoning effort `high`.

### 🧰 Setup (#536, #542)
- **`EvoSci setup`** — one command that prepares what EvoScientist needs beyond the Python package. `--manifest`, `--json` and `--stage <id>` print a staged JSON progress stream for the upcoming desktop app and install scripts.
- **Node.js** — a system Node 20+ with `npx` is used as is; otherwise a private Node 24 LTS is installed into `~/.evoscientist/tools/` and put first on `PATH` only inside EvoScientist's own processes. It is also installed on demand when the WebUI, an `npx` MCP server or onboarding needs it, so pip and uv users who never run `EvoSci setup` are covered. No shell rc file, nvm, fnm or conda install is touched.
- **Research Python** — when no usable `python` is on `PATH` (uv tool installs, stock macOS, many Linux distributions), setup builds `~/.evoscientist/envs/default` with numpy, pandas, matplotlib and scipy for the agent's shell. Your own `python` (conda, venv, system) always wins; without either, EvoScientist shows one hint to run `EvoSci setup`.
- **`--cn`** — Node downloads come from npmmirror and pip packages from the Tsinghua index, saved as `mirror: cn` so later runs keep the same source. Thanks @jfilipiuk!

### 🧠 Memory (#553)
- **Profile memory degrades per file** — once `SOUL.md`, `USER_PROFILE.md`, `RESEARCH_TASTE.md` and the project profile together passed the 24,000-character prompt budget, none of them reached the model, so rules in `SOUL.md` silently stopped applying. Now every file that fits its share stays whole, only an oversized file is shortened to its head and tail with a pointer to the full file, and a warning names it. The budget is raised to 60,000 characters.
- **Newest observations first** — the inline observation index was ordered by content hash, so once it filled up, which observations the agent saw at a glance was effectively random. It now lists the newest first; older ones drop off the end and stay reachable through `search_observations`.

### 📦 Dependencies
- deepagents 0.7.21; lock refresh: anthropic SDK 1.11.0, openai SDK 3.24.0, langchain-core 1.6.6, langchain-openai 1.6.7, langchain-anthropic 1.7.5.

## What's Changed
* Add EvoSci setup with a staged JSON protocol and the Node stage (#516) by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/536
* Add the research-env setup stage and use it when no python is on PATH (#517) by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/542
* release: v0.3.5 by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/553


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/compare/v0.3.4...v0.3.5

# EvoScientist v0.3.4 — Claude Sonnet 5.5, Shell-Agnostic WebUI Launcher & Native DeepSeek Memory Fix

G'Day! v0.3.4 adds **Claude Sonnet 5.5** on Anthropic and OpenRouter, turns the **WebUI launcher into a shell-agnostic core** as groundwork for the desktop app, fixes **local-server detection behind a system proxy** on Windows, and gets **memory workers and scheduled-task grading working on native DeepSeek**. Under the hood: a routine dependency refresh (anthropic SDK 1.9, openai SDK 3.20, langchain 1.4.3), with deepagents unchanged at 0.7.19.

---

### 🔌 Models (#535)
- **Claude Sonnet 5.5** — `claude-sonnet-5-5` (Anthropic) and `claude-sonnet-5.5` (OpenRouter).
- **New Claude models work out of the box** — a Claude model newer than langchain-anthropic's model table now gets adaptive thinking at max effort, its full 128K output budget and native structured output automatically, so memory workers and rubric grading work on it from day one, including behind the OAuth proxy.
- **Known limit** — through OpenRouter, Sonnet 5.5 cannot grade scheduled-task rubrics (it rejects forced tool use, and its JSON mode rejects the grader schema); EvoScientist now warns when it is set as the grader model. Use the native Anthropic route or another auxiliary model. Tool selection above 42 tools recovers on its own: after one rejected request it switches to automatic tool choice.

### 🖥️ WebUI & desktop groundwork (#504)
- **Shell-agnostic launcher** — WebUI start, health check and teardown are now a reusable core that the terminal command and upcoming desktop shells drive; `EvoSci --ui webui` behaves as before.
- **Busy check** — `GET /api/bg_processes/running` lists running background jobs, and a busy check detects in-flight runs, ready for the desktop app and `EvoSci update`.
- **Windows** — the local langgraph dev server is detected as healthy behind a system proxy or VPN, terminal Ctrl+C no longer reaches it, and the `EvoSci server stop` command printed for PowerShell works when pasted. Thanks @jfilipiuk!

### 🧠 Memory & scheduler (#533)
- **Native DeepSeek** — memory workers and scheduled-task rubric grading now use tool-calling structured output on native DeepSeek, which rejects the JSON-schema response format they sent before.

### 📦 Dependencies
- Lock refresh: anthropic SDK 1.9.0, openai SDK 3.20.0, langchain 1.4.3; deepagents stays at 0.7.19.

## What's Changed
* Shell-agnostic WebUI launcher, busy check and langgraph dev fixes (#515) by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/504
* fix: use tool-calling structured output on native DeepSeek by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/533

# EvoScientist v0.3.3 — Codex OAuth End to End, Human-Only HITL Limits & Per-Run Summarization

G'Day! v0.3.3 makes **Codex OAuth for ChatGPT Plus/Pro work end to end**, shows **reasoning from vLLM-style endpoints**, counts **HITL round limits only when a human was actually asked**, and lets **summarization follow the model each run really uses**. Scheduled-task rubrics now grade on OpenRouter's OpenAI models, and each surface can pick its gateway backend. Under the hood: deepagents 0.7.19 and a full dependency refresh.

---

### 🔐 Codex OAuth (#506)
- **ChatGPT Plus/Pro works end to end** — ccproxy settings now reach the server as environment overrides (its `--config` flag was ignored), so the model you configure is the model that runs.
- **No more `apply_patch` refusals** — ccproxy's injected Codex CLI prompt is turned off; models edit files with EvoScientist's own tools.
- **Codex client version** — a failed `codex --version` probe no longer pins an old fallback that the backend rejects for newer models.
- **Workspace `.env` keys** no longer undo OAuth routing.
- **Upgrade note** — stop a ccproxy started by an older EvoScientist once (`pkill -f "ccproxy serve"`) so the new settings load. A model your plan does not serve now fails with a 400 naming that model. The `oauth` extra requires `ccproxy-api>=0.2.10`.

### 🧠 Reasoning & context (#506, #493)
- **Reasoning from vLLM-style endpoints** — OpenAI-compatible servers that stream reasoning under `reasoning` (not `reasoning_content`) now show their thinking.
- **Summarization follows the run's model** — when a run overrides its model (`configurable.model`, e.g. async sub-agents following the caller), the summarization trigger and overflow limits use that model's context window instead of the one the graph was built with. Thanks @NkAntony777!

### 🛑 Human-in-the-loop (#494)
- **Round limits count only human prompts** — long unattended turns under "approve all" or the allow-list no longer stop at 50 rounds; the limit applies only to rounds that actually asked you, on the Rich CLI, the TUI and channels, and the parked checkpoint is closed cleanly when it is reached. Thanks @NkAntony777!

### ⏰ Scheduler (#531)
- **Rubric grading on OpenRouter OpenAI models** — the grader now uses tool calling for `openai/` models; OpenAI's strict JSON mode rejected the grader schema with a 400.
- **Media the grader's model cannot read** is replaced with a placeholder before the call, matching deepagents 0.7.19's setup.

### 🧩 Experts (#505)
- **Background experts on Python 3.13** — async expert dispatch no longer trips a blocking-call error on its first model call; CI now also tests Python 3.13.

### 🛰️ Gateway (#470, #492)
- **Per-surface gateway backend** — `serve`, single-shot and standalone channels follow `gateway_backend`, while the CLI and TUI opt in per surface; everything stays `local` by default. Thanks @jfilipiuk!
- **Server gateway** registers a new thread before its pre-run state read. Thanks @NkAntony777!

### 📦 Dependencies
- **deepagents 0.7.19** — rejected `read_file` media recovers with a placeholder, unsupported content is filtered by a dedicated middleware, tool-offload paths are bounded. Floor raised to `~=0.7.19`.
- Full lock refresh: langchain-anthropic 1.7.4, langchain-openai 1.6.6, langchain-core 1.6.5, langgraph-api 0.15.1, openai SDK 3.19.2.

## What's Changed
* fix(experts): compose async expert prompt off the event loop by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/505
* fix: register the server-gateway thread before the pre-run state read by @NkAntony777 in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/492
* fix: track the per-run model context window in the summarization middleware by @NkAntony777 in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/493
* fix(llm): make Codex OAuth usable end-to-end and capture vLLM-style reasoning by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/506
* refactor: route production surfaces through the configured gateway backend by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/470
* fix: cap HITL resume loops on human-prompted rounds only by @NkAntony777 in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/494
* release: v0.3.3 by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/531

body.body:
# EvoScientist v0.3.1 — Multilingual Memory Search, GLM-5.3-FlashX & the Server Gateway Groundwork

G'Day! v0.3.1 is a consolidation release on the 0.3 line. Memory search now **works for Chinese and other languages written without word spaces**, the model list gains **GLM-5.3-FlashX** and **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash**, and Stage 1–2 of the **LangGraph server gateway** lands behind an opt-in flag — the groundwork for running the CLI against a served graph — together with a **unified HITL approval policy** and a fix for a **model fallback chain** that sub-agent graph builds could overwrite. Under the hood the stack moves to **deepagents 0.7.15** on a fully refreshed lockfile (anthropic SDK 1.7, openai SDK 3.16, langgraph-api 0.14.3).

---

### 🧠 Memory — multilingual observation search (#485)

- **Queries without word spaces now rank properly** — the tokenizer emits overlapping bigrams for CJK, kana, Hangul and Thai and keeps other non-ASCII words whole, so a Chinese query no longer produces zero tokens and falls back to literal matching (which missed memories whenever the words appeared in a different order). Single-character CJK runs stay excluded to avoid broad matches; Cyrillic terms move from substring fallback to whole-word ranked matching; ASCII behaviour (three-character minimum, underscore handling) is unchanged. Thanks @din0s.

### 🔌 Providers & models (#483, #487)

- **GLM-5.3-FlashX (Zhipu + OpenRouter)** — the 200 tokens/s tier of GLM-5.3-Flash, 1M context. Not offered on the Zhipu Coding Plan yet, so it is not listed under `zhipu-code`.
- **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepSeek + OpenRouter)** — including the rolling native `deepseek-flash` tier.
- **GLM context windows match by family** — `glm-5.3` / `glm-5.2` are resolved ahead of the 203K `glm-5` fallback, so future `glm-5.3-*` variants get their 1M window without a registry edit.

### 🛰️ LangGraph server gateway — Stage 1–2, opt-in (#434, #437–#443)

- **New `gateway_backend` flag** (`local` | `langgraph_server`, default `local`) — nothing changes unless you turn it on. With `langgraph_server`, the served graph spawns in full deploy mode and refuses to reuse a stripped keepalive leftover.
- **Per-run model and recursion limit** — on the server backend `/model` sends `configurable.model` / `model_provider` per run instead of rebuilding the graph, and `recursion_limit` is forwarded as a first-class run config key.
- **Middleware events cross the process boundary** — tool-selection and fallback narration reach clients on the server backend.
- **Completions read from thread state** — async sub-agent completions and background-process exits are detected from thread state, identically on both backends; the state read path is now the sole async-task completion path.
- **Model fallback chain fix** — graph builds no longer overwrite the module-global chain (previously the last of the sub-agent graph builds won); it is seeded lazily from config on first read, and `/model-fallback` edits still persist. A CI-enforced contract test now classifies how every config field reaches the served graph. Thanks @jfilipiuk for the whole stack.

### 🛡️ HITL — one approval policy (#444)

- **Always armed, suppressed per run** — the main graph is always armed for `execute` / `run_in_background` / `schedule_task`, and auto mode disarms per run rather than per graph. The dangerous-command backend guard is derived per call from the same signal, so a mid-session `auto_approve` flip never leaves a stale guard; auto-approve sessions suppress the interrupt and keep backend guarding. Sub-agent graphs stay unarmed at construction.
- **TUI now honours `shell_allow_list`** — the TUI approval flow routes through the same `resolve_action_decision` policy as the Rich CLI and channels, closing a gap where allow-listed commands still prompted there. The same policy is served over HTTP for non-Python clients. Thanks @jfilipiuk.

### 📦 Dependencies

- **deepagents 0.7.15** (from 0.7.13) — `read_file` results now carry a `@@ lines A-B of T | next offset N @@` status header above verbatim source instead of a line-number gutter, which removes a common source of `edit_file` mismatches; summarization gains an input budget that compacts before the provider rejects the request and surfaces an irreducible overflow as a clean `ContextOverflowError`. The floor is aligned to `~=0.7.15` so upgraders get it too.
- **Full lockfile refresh** — anthropic SDK 1.7, openai SDK 3.16, langgraph-api 0.14.3, langchain 1.4.2, langsmith 0.13.0.
- **Caps unchanged** — `openrouter<0.11.0`, `textual<8.2.7` (8.2.8 still breaks CJK input on Kitty-protocol terminals), `mcp<2`.

## What's Changed
* feat(models): add deepseek-v4.1-flash (openrouter) and deepseek-flash (native) by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/483
* feat: harden LangGraph server gateway for production cutover (Stage 1) by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/434
* feat: fix the model fallback chain and pin the tool-binding contract by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/437
* feat: spawn the gateway backend in full mode behind a flag by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/438
* refactor: send model and recursion limit per run instead of rebuilding the graph by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/439
* feat: bridge middleware events across the process boundary by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/440
* refactor: read async sub-agent completions from thread state by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/441
* refactor: make the state read path the sole async-task completion path by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/442
* feat: mirror background-process lifecycle into thread state by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/443
* fix(memory): improve multilingual observation search tokenization by @din0s in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/485
* refactor: always arm HITL and route approval through a shared policy by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/444
* release: v0.3.1 by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/487


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/compare/v0.3.0...v0.3.1

body.body:
# EvoScientist v0.3.0 — Model-Faithful Async Sub-Agents, Live Expert Install & MiniMax Replay Fix

G'Day! v0.3.0 opens the 0.3 line. Async sub-agents now **inherit the model of the run that launched them** instead of silently falling back to the config default, experts installed mid-session **dispatch in the background without `/new`**, and the **MiniMax second-turn crash** on the Anthropic-compatible endpoint is gone, alongside two smaller fixes in channel retries and OpenRouter attribution. Under the hood the stack moves to **langchain-quickjs 0.3.7** (PTC tool calls inside `code_interpreter` now stream live) and **langgraph-api 0.14** on a fully refreshed lockfile, with **deepagents 0.7.13** unchanged.

---

### 🤝 Async sub-agents — caller model inheritance (#446)

- **Launch and update both inherit the caller's model** — `start_async_task` and `update_async_task` publish the launching run's `(model, model_provider)` from `runtime.config` to a request-scoped ContextVar, and the single `runs.create` merge point layers it over the config default as the highest-precedence source. A WebUI run on a free or cheap model no longer dispatches writing / data-analysis on the config default (and no longer 402s when that account is out of credit). Runs with no per-run override behave exactly as before. Thanks @jfilipiuk.

### 🧑‍🔬 Experts — install now, dispatch now (#420)

- **Resolve-on-miss at the dispatch boundary** — when `start_async_task` sees an unknown `subagent_type`, one walk of the skills tree adds every not-yet-known expert to the dispatch map *and* the completion watcher's map before the request is rejected. An expert installed via `/install-skill` in the current session is reachable in the same turn; the `<active_expert>` cue and dispatch can no longer disagree. Existing entries are never overwritten, and the walk uses the config the agent was built with, so a mid-session port change cannot spec a new expert onto the wrong dev-server port. Thanks @jfilipiuk.

### 🔌 Providers — MiniMax replay fix (#449)

- **Mixed string + typed content blocks now replay** — MiniMax's Anthropic-compatible endpoint returns assistant content that mixes bare strings with typed thinking / tool blocks; replaying that history crashed the next turn with `string indices must be integers`. The Anthropic history normalizer now wraps string items as text blocks while preserving typed blocks. Applies to every Anthropic-routed provider (MiniMax, Kimi Coding, custom Anthropic endpoints). Closes #448. Thanks @mikemikimike.

### 📨 Channels — honest retry classification (#394)

- **Non-retryable errors are no longer retried** — `Channel._extract_retry_after()` returned `1.0` for any exception, so generic failures were re-sent as if rate-limited. It now returns `None` unless the error carries an explicit `retry_after` or is a 429, in which case the previous back-off is unchanged. Thanks @neverbiasu.

### 🧭 OpenRouter attribution (#453)

- **`openrouter_app_title` only takes effect with a custom `openrouter_http_referer`** — OpenRouter keys app pages by referer and `X-Title` renames that page, so a title-only override renamed the shared public EvoScientist app page. The default title is now forced whenever the referer is the default; forks that override both are unaffected.

### 📦 Dependencies

- **langchain-quickjs 0.3.7** — upstream now streams PTC tool calls natively: `tools.*` calls made from inside a `code_interpreter` eval run with the outer run's callbacks, so the CLI/TUI shows each of them as its own tool row next to the running `code_interpreter` call (previously invisible until the eval returned). In-eval `task()` fan-out still reports through the `custom` subagent channel, so the TUI dispatch panel and the WebUI Dynamic Workflow panel are unchanged, and no synthetic messages enter the thread and keys the REPL slot by a private `_quickjs_slot_id` state field instead of `thread_id`, which also keeps that private state out of sub-agent propagation. The shutdown path and the slot-eviction regression test follow the new slot API, and `langchain-quickjs>=0.3.7` is now declared directly — deepagents' own floor is 0.3.5, so fresh installs were already on 0.3.7 while the shutdown cleanup still reached for a 0.3.6 attribute.
- **deepagents 0.7.13** — unchanged; still the latest release.
- **Lockfile refresh** — langgraph-api 0.14.0 (runtime-inmem 0.34.0), openai SDK 3.13, anthropic SDK 1.5, langchain-core 1.6.3, langchain-anthropic 1.7.2, langchain-openai 1.6.2, mcp 1.30.0. Full suite and a live `langgraph dev` in full mode verified on the exact lock.


## What's Changed
* fix(llm): honor openrouter_app_title only alongside a custom referer by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/453
* fix: _extract_retry_after returns None for non-retryable errors by @neverbiasu in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/394
* feat: dispatch newly installed experts in the background without /new by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/420
* fix: normalize string blocks in Anthropic history by @mikemikimike in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/449
* feat: inherit the caller's model for async sub-agent launch and update by @jfilipiuk in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/446
* release: v0.3.0 by @X-iZhang in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/462

## New Contributors
* @neverbiasu made their first contribution in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/394
* @mikemikimike made their first contribution in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/449

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/compare/v0.2.10...v0.3.0

# EvoScientist v0.2.10 — Frontier Models, First-Contact Profiles & Scheduler Rubrics

G'Day! v0.2.10 brings four **frontier models** into the registry — **Claude Fable 5.1**, **GPT-6 Astra**, **Gemini 3.8 Flash**, and **Meta Muse Spark 1.3** — teaches the agent to **introduce itself and remember who you are** on first contact, lets scheduled tasks carry an **acceptance checklist** that is graded before a run counts as done, and moves the stack to **deepagents 0.7.13** on a fully refreshed lockfile.

---

### 🔌 Providers & models

- **Claude Fable 5.1** — `claude-fable-5-1` on Anthropic, `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` on OpenRouter. 1M context via the `claude-` family rule.
- **GPT-6 Astra** — `gpt-6-astra` on OpenAI, `openai/gpt-6-astra` on OpenRouter. New `gpt-6` family entry (1.05M context) so future GPT-6 variants resolve without a patch.
- **Gemini 3.8 Flash** — `gemini-3.8-flash` on Google, `google/gemini-3.8-flash` on OpenRouter. 1.05M context via the `gemini-3` family rule.
- **Meta Muse Spark 1.3** — `meta/muse-spark-1.3` on OpenRouter. New `muse-spark` family entry (1M context) covering 1.1/1.2/1.3.

### 🧠 Memory — first-contact profile bootstrap (#450)

- `USER_PROFILE.md` now carries a YAML frontmatter (`name`, `field`, `homepage`, `intro`) alongside the prose profile. While `name` is empty, the main agent's first turn of a thread asks who you are and what you work on, records the answers, and stops asking; declining (`intro: skipped`) also stops it. Unanswered asks back off exponentially (sessions 1, 2, 4, 8, …) instead of nagging every thread.
- Off in `auto_mode` and never on sub-agents or the memory workers.

### ⏰ Scheduler — rubric acceptance checklist (#451)

- `/schedule add <cron> "<prompt>" --rubric "<checklist>"` (and the `schedule_task` tool's `rubric` argument) attaches an optional acceptance checklist to a scheduled task. After each run the auxiliary model grades the workspace against the checklist with read-only file tools; a failing grade sends the run back for one revision before it is accepted, and a checklist that cannot be graded ends the run with `grader_error` rather than a silent pass. Tasks without a rubric behave exactly as before.
- Known limit: `anthropic/claude-fable-5.1` via OpenRouter cannot act as the grader (the route rejects both structured-output strategies); native Anthropic and other OpenRouter routes work.

- The LLM tool selector now engages only when the main agent has more than **42** tools (was 26). The base tool set has grown to 24 (29 with async task tools), so the old threshold triggered an extra selection call on every turn even without MCP servers; the new one keeps stock installs and light MCP setups on the direct path and reserves selection for large tool sets.

# EvoScientist v0.2.7 — Faster Starts, Hardened Channels

G'Day! v0.2.7 is a quality release: **startup gets noticeably faster** across the CLI, `langgraph dev`, and thread listing, four new models land (**Gemini 3.7 Flash**, **DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813**, **Grok 4.6**, **GLM-5.3**), **encrypted-webhook channels stop accepting unsigned posts**, and a batch of fixes lands for MCP stdio servers on Windows, sub-agent tool resolution, and `/compact` history offloading on **deepagents 0.7.6**.

---

### ⚡ Startup performance (#407)

- **Lazy import surface** — heavy dependencies (langchain chat models, langgraph, textual) load on first use instead of at process start; `evosci --help` and the onboarding wizard start in a fraction of the time.
- **langgraph dev keepalive** — with `langgraph_dev_keepalive` enabled, the managed `langgraph dev` server stays alive after the CLI exits and is reused by the next session in the same workspace (seconds → near-instant reattach); a sidecar ownership protocol reclaims stale servers safely.
- **Indexed thread listing** — `/threads` and the resume picker use a covering index instead of walking full checkpoints.

### 🔌 Models

- **Gemini 3.7 Flash** — Google's new workhorse flagship (GA, 1M context, tunable thinking levels), selectable in `EvoSci onboard` and `/model` on Google GenAI and OpenRouter.
- **DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813** — the GA snapshot of DeepSeek's flagship MoE (1M context), selectable on OpenRouter alongside the existing undated `deepseek-v4-pro`.
- **Grok 4.6** — xAI's agent-focused frontier model (500K context, reasoning-effort levels), selectable on OpenRouter.
- **GLM-5.3** — Zhipu's new flagship (1M context, 128K output, tunable thinking), selectable on the Zhipu general + Coding Plan endpoints and OpenRouter.

### 🛡 Channel webhook hardening (#401)

- Channels configured with webhook encryption/signing now **reject unsigned POSTs (403)** instead of silently accepting plaintext deliveries — closes the mismatch where a platform configured for encryption could still drive the agent with unauthenticated requests.

### 🛠 Fixes

- **MCP stdio servers under redirected streams** (#423) — stdio subprocesses now always get a real stderr file descriptor; fixes `Errno 9` startup failures on Windows when EvoScientist runs with redirected output (serve mode, schedulers, CI).
- **Sub-agent tools resolve at dispatch time** (#381) — tool names from sub-agent YAML are kept until the sync/async execution decision, so async sub-agents keep their remote-registered tools and config load no longer emits misleading tool warnings.

Wire-level tests guard the offload path against future API drift.

# EvoScientist v0.2.6 — Agent Teams

G'Day! v0.2.6 is a feature release: **agent teams** land — installed skills that ship an actor definition become invitable experts you can consult in-turn, fan out in parallel panels, or dispatch as background jobs. Alongside: **configurable bind hosts** with safe loopback defaults, the **Volcengine Coding Plan** provider, **Qwen3.8-Max**, and **deepagents 0.7.5**.

---

### 🤝 Agent teams (#369, #370, #371, #391, #404)

- **Experts via `AGENTS.md`** — a skill directory with an `AGENTS.md` next to its `SKILL.md` becomes an invitable expert: the `AGENTS.md` body is the actor definition (persona + result-envelope contract) and becomes the expert's runtime system prompt, while `SKILL.md` stays pure knowledge readable off the `/skills/` mount. Legacy `type: expert` frontmatter still works (deprecated, one-time warning).
- **Invite per session** — `/experts` lists installed experts; `/expert <name>` invites or dismisses one (case-insensitive, tab-completed); `/expert clear` dismisses all. Invitations are session-scoped: `/new` and switching threads via `/resume` dismiss them with an announcement. The WebUI gets the same feature via its expert gallery (`GET /api/teams`).
- **Three dispatch modes, orchestrator's choice** — in-turn consult (`task` tool), parallel expert panels via in-eval `task()` fan-out rendered live in a TUI panel widget (per-dispatch spinner, elapsed time, status), or background jobs via `start_async_task` that return a structured result envelope (output path, summary, expert-defined metadata). Invited experts bias delegation through an `<active_expert>` prompt block — the agent can still just read the skill and do the work itself.
- First-party experts ship from the [EvoSkills](https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoSkills) repo; a freshly installed expert becomes dispatchable after `/new` (the `/expert` command reminds you).

### 🛡 Configurable bind hosts (#402, #412)

- **`langgraph_dev_host` / `webui_host`** config keys plus `--host` flags on `EvoSci`, `EvoSci serve`, and `EvoSci deploy` — both default to loopback `127.0.0.1`; pass `--host 0.0.0.0` to reach the servers from another machine on a trusted network.
- **Public binds warn loudly** — any non-loopback bind prints a red `PUBLIC BIND` banner (the servers are unauthenticated and the agent can run shell). Internal health probes and async self-dispatch always stay on loopback regardless of the bind.
- LAN WebUI use requires widening **both** hosts (the browser talks to the backend directly) — the launcher prints the exact `config set` hint when only the front-end is public. Pairs with the `@evoscientist/webui` 0.2.3 origin fix, which arrives automatically via `npx @latest`.

### 🔌 Providers

- **Volcengine Coding Plan** (#411) — new `volcengine-code` provider with `glm-5.2` and `kimi-k2.5` aliases, selectable in `EvoSci onboard` and `/model`; shares the regular `VOLCENGINE_API_KEY`.
- **Qwen3.8-Max** — Alibaba's new flagship (1M context), selectable on DashScope, the DashScope Coding Plan, and OpenRouter.

### 📦 deepagents 0.7.5

- **Unsupported media becomes placeholders, not 400s** — media in `read_file` results that the current model can't accept (per its capability profile) is replaced with a clean text placeholder instead of triggering a non-retryable provider 400; e.g. reading back a generated `.pptx` on Anthropic used to kill the whole thread. Models without profile data (custom endpoints) pass through unchanged — verified across the full provider zoo, no behavior change on custom routes.
- **Machine-readable exit codes** — `execute` tool results now carry the exit code in the message artifact alongside the output text.
- Degenerate `read_file` windows (`limit=0`, negative offsets) return clean empty reads instead of a tool error; pulls in `langchain-anthropic` 1.5.4.

### 🛠 Fixes

- **Blank tool-call IDs repaired** (#399) — providers that stream empty `tool_call_id`s (notably Kimi and Zhipu) no longer freeze the session with an HTTP 400 after a tool round; blank ids are normalized before each model request.

# EvoScientist v0.2.5 — Unified HITL approval & deepagents 0.7.0

G'Day! v0.2.5 is a safety-and-foundation release: **human-in-the-loop approval now covers every sub-agent tier** — sync and async — under one consistent policy, and the framework moves to **deepagents 0.7.0** with leaner prompts and a gated `delete` tool. Two new LLM providers round it out.

---

### 🛡 Unified HITL approval (#396)

- **Sync sub-agents now prompt** — declarative sub-agents (planner / research / code / debug) inherit the same native `interrupt_on=` gating as the main agent for `execute`, `run_in_background`, `schedule_task`, and the new `delete`. Previously only the main agent asked.
- **Async agents can't hang on un-resumable interrupts** — `writing-agent` / `data-analysis-agent` instead get a backend guard that refuses the dangerous pipe-into-interpreter set (`curl | bash`-style) and **relays the refusal back to the orchestrator**, so the main agent can adjust course or ask you.
- **Parallel interrupts no longer crash** — approvals resume **one interrupt at a time, keyed by id**; parallel sub-agents each raising an `execute` approval used to trip langgraph's multi-pending-interrupt crash.
- **Allow-list hardening** — `shell_allow_list` now matches **per command segment**, so `allowed-cmd && anything-else` can't ride an allow-listed prefix; clobbering redirects (`>|`, `2>|`) are covered too.
- **One policy engine** — `resolve_action_decision` (precedence: `dangerous_mode` > dangerous-pattern detection > `auto_approve` > allow-list) backs the Rich CLI, TUI, and channel approval prompts alike; `auto_approve` now short-circuits on the channel path as well.

### 📦 deepagents 0.7.0 (#395)

- **Leaner built-in prompts** — framework prompt overhead down ~65% in input tokens.
- **New `delete` tool, gated** — recursive file deletion ships upstream; EvoScientist puts it behind the **same approval as `execute`** (always prompts — never allow-listed), skips prompts in auto/dangerous modes, and hard-blocks it on read-only, memory, and autoskills backends as well as async sub-agents.
- **Todos kept** — upstream made `TodoListMiddleware` opt-in; EvoScientist re-mounts it explicitly so `write_todos` planning keeps working everywhere.

### 🔌 New providers

- **Requesty** (#346) and **Atlas Cloud** (#388) — selectable in `EvoSci onboard` and `/model`.

### 🛠 Fixes

- **Unnamed tool calls filtered** (#390, #393) — malformed tool-call entries without a name no longer 400 the API on history replay; vetting is hardened on raw paths, and the tool-history repair middleware now also mounts on sync sub-agents.
- **Deploy port propagation** (#385) — the `langgraph dev` bind port is forwarded into the subprocess env, so the async self-loop URL follows a non-default `--port`.

### 🔧 Internals

- **Owned async runtime** (#376) — the CLI's async bridges (event loops, executors, watchers) are centralized under one owned runtime; shutdown drain dropped from ~8s to ~3s.

---

# EvoScientist v0.2.4 — Claude Opus 5, new Geminis & the Anthropic-protocol channel

G'Day! v0.2.4 is a model-catalog and protocol-compat release: **Claude Opus 5** and two new **Gemini** flashes join the lineup, and **Kimi K3 now works end-to-end over Anthropic-protocol channels** — including the Kimi For Coding subscription endpoint — after a deep dive into how strict Anthropic-compatible edges validate requests.

---

### 🧠 New models

- **Claude Opus 5** — selectable in `EvoSci onboard` and `/model` on **Anthropic** (native `claude-opus-5`) and **OpenRouter** (`anthropic/claude-opus-5`, fast variant included), with 1M context.
- **Claude 5-series thinking fix** — `claude-opus-5` / `claude-sonnet-5` on the direct Anthropic API now get **adaptive thinking**; the auto-config previously fell through to the legacy `budget_tokens` shape, which 5-series models reject with HTTP 400.
- **Gemini 3.6 Flash & Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite** — selectable on **Google** (native) and **OpenRouter**, 1M context.

---

### 🧭 Kimi K3 over Anthropic-protocol channels

K3 runs with thinking always on, and strict Anthropic-compatible edges (Moonshot's Kimi For Coding endpoint, OpenRouter's Anthropic schema) reject several things the default request path produced. v0.2.4 makes the whole surface work:

- **Structured output no longer 400s** — `with_structured_output` on K3-class models routes through `output_config.format` (json_schema) instead of a forced tool call, which mandatory-thinking endpoints reject (`tool_choice 'specified' is incompatible with thinking enabled`). This also fixes the >20-tools tool-selector on these channels.
- **Cross-provider history replay** — switching a session from an OpenAI-compatible provider (Qwen, DeepSeek, …) to an Anthropic-protocol endpoint no longer 400s: foreign `reasoning_content` blocks are stripped before send. Native Claude benefits from the same protection.
- **Multi-turn thinking preserved** — K3's thinking blocks are kept on replay (Kimi backends require them on tool-call turns), and streamed thinking that arrives without a `signature_delta` gets its signature defaulted — fixing a second-turn 400 after any streamed reply.

# EvoScientist v0.2.1 — AutoSkills: skills the agent writes for itself

G'Day! v0.2.1 builds straight on the **autonomy milestone** from v0.2.0. Last release taught EvoScientist to run on its own schedule and organize its own memory; this one closes the loop — the agent now **turns that memory into reusable skills**. The headline is **AutoSkills** (#319): a background worker periodically mines your observation clusters and drafts new skills, handed to you as proposals you review with `/autoskills`. Rounding it out is a new **`--output-format stream-json`** headless output mode for programmatic / SDK clients (#309), new model support (**Claude Sonnet 5**, **GLM-5.2**), plus completion, Windows, and TUI fixes and a dependency bump.

---

### 🛠️ AutoSkills

EvoMemory can now author its own skills from what it has learned (#319).

- **Learns skills from memory** — a slow background worker scans your accumulated observation clusters (the self-linking memory graph from v0.2.0) and drafts reusable `SKILL.md` skills out of the patterns it keeps seeing.
- **You stay in control** — by default it runs in **review mode**: drafts land as proposals you inspect and accept/deny with `/autoskills` (`ls` / `accept` / `deny` / `now`). Prefer hands-off? Switch to **auto-install** mode and approved skills go straight into your user skills dir.
- **On its own cadence** — runs on a built-in schedule (**weekly at 03:00** by default; switch to `nightly` / `monthly` or set a custom time) through the managed `langgraph dev` server, as an 8th async graph. Toggle the whole feature with `/autoskills on|off`.

---

### 🧩 Headless `stream-json` output

A new machine-readable output mode for driving EvoScientist headlessly (#309).

- **`EvoSci -p "…" --output-format stream-json`** emits EvoScientist's native event stream as line-delimited JSON (JSONL) on stdout — one self-describing object per line.
- **Clean protocol** — stdout is pure JSONL; all human output (status lines, panels) goes to stderr. The stream ends with a `done` event carrying the final response; unknown event types are safe to ignore (forward-compatible by design).
- **Unattended by default** — headless runs enable `--auto-mode` automatically (opt out with `--no-auto-mode`). Full event-schema contract and an example transcript live in `docs/stream-json.md`.

---

### 🧠 New models

- **Claude Sonnet 5** — added to the **Anthropic** and **OpenRouter** providers.
- **GLM-5.2** — added across **NVIDIA**, **OpenRouter**, **SiliconFlow**, and **Zhipu / Zhipu CodePlan**, with its **1M** context window registered (an exception to the 203K `glm-5` family default).

Both show up in the `EvoSci onboard` model picker for their respective providers.

---

### 🐛 Fixes & 🧩 Dependencies

- **Richer slash-command completions** — improved multi-stage completion behavior, duplicate-view and tab-handling fixes (#302).
- **Windows UTF-8 config** — config files are now read and written as UTF-8, fixing garbled reads on Windows (#318).
- **TUI welcome banner** — stays pinned at the top after `/new` (and after a short turn that fits the viewport) instead of dropping out of view — a regression from the free-scrolling anchor change (#311, closes #301).

# EvoScientist v0.2.0 — Scheduled Tasks, Self-Linking Memory & the Autonomy Milestone

G'Day! v0.2.0 is the **autonomy milestone** — EvoScientist steps from an on-demand assistant toward an always-on research buddy that runs on its own schedule and organizes its own memory. The headline is **Scheduled Tasks** — cron-style recurring runs you set up with `/schedule` or plain language and let run unattended, with shell-access gating for safety — paired with **self-linking memory** that connects related observations into a knowledge graph instead of a flat log. Rounding it out: a read-only **`GET /api/models`** endpoint that powers the WebUI model picker, a **tool-selector fix** that keeps the main agent's memory always reachable, and a **deepagents 0.6.12 / langchain-quickjs 0.3.2** dependency bump.

---

### ⏰ Scheduled Tasks

EvoScientist can now schedule its own work and run unattended (#306).

- **Set it in seconds** — `/schedule` (add / list / remove / run / pause / resume), or just ask in plain language ("every weekday at 9am, summarize new arXiv papers on diffusion models") and the agent schedules it for you.
- **Runs on its own** — a dedicated, general-purpose scheduler agent fires on a cron timetable through the managed `langgraph dev` server and reports results back through the same completion notifier as async sub-agents.
- **Safe by default** — a scheduler shell-gate blocks `execute` in unattended runs unless you explicitly allow it, so a cron job can't silently run shell commands while you're away.

---

### 🧠 Self-Linking Memory

Memory no longer stores observations in isolation — it connects them (#307).

- **Typed connections** — after each run, related observations are linked with typed edges (**complements / contradicts / supersedes**), turning the memory store into a navigable knowledge graph.
- **Coherent as it grows** — links use stable observation IDs and are written per batch, so the graph stays consistent across sessions.
- **Leaner design** — replaces the earlier knowledge-synthesis layer with a lower-cost linking step, with no separate knowledge index to maintain.

---

### 🌐 Model Registry API

A new read-only endpoint exposes the model registry over HTTP (#308).

- **`GET /api/models`** — returns the available models (provider → models) as JSON.
- **Powers the WebUI** — drives the model picker, and lets any SDK / external client discover what's available.
- **Read-only** — no writes; served by the `langgraph dev` process.

---

### 🐛 Fixes & 🧩 Dependencies

- **Tool-selector** — the main agent now always keeps its memory tools available even when the LLM tool-selector trims the visible toolset, so memory stays reachable on every turn (#305).
- **deepagents 0.6.12 / langchain-quickjs 0.3.2** — picks up the summarization media-reference fix; pulls langchain-core 1.4.8 / langchain 1.3.11 / langchain-anthropic 1.4.8.

---

# EvoScientist v0.1.9 — 🚨 Urgent Fresh-Install Hotfix

> ⚠️ **Update now if you installed or upgraded to v0.1.8.** Every fresh install of v0.1.8 is broken — the agent crashes on the **very first message**, in the CLI, TUI, and every channel. v0.1.9 is the fix and changes nothing else.

G'Day! v0.1.9 is a one-line emergency hotfix for a crash that took down **fresh installs of v0.1.8**: the first message errored out with ``The subagent `task` tool cannot be exposed via `ptc` ``. Existing environments with an older pinned `deepagents` were unaffected — which is exactly why it slipped past local testing.

---

### 🐛 The Crash

EvoScientist's code-interpreter middleware exposes a curated set of read-only, batchable tools inside the JavaScript REPL (its "PTC allowlist"), and `task` (sub-agent dispatch) used to be one of them.

`deepagents` 0.6.11 ships `langchain-quickjs` 0.3, which now **reserves `task` as the top-level `task()` REPL global** (with `subagentType` + `responseSchema` support) and raises if `task` also appears in the `ptc` allowlist — a `tools.task` variant would be a conflicting duplicate that silently drops `responseSchema`.

Because v0.1.8's dependency range (`deepagents[quickjs]~=0.6.10`) allows 0.6.11, every **new** `uv tool install` / `pip install` resolved to the breaking 0.6.11 + quickjs 0.3 and crashed on the first agent turn. Pre-existing installs kept their older locked `deepagents` and ran fine — so the regression was invisible in development until reproduced against the versions users actually receive.

### ✅ The Fix

- **Removed `task` from the code-interpreter PTC allowlist.** `task()` is still fully available as the REPL global (now correctly preserving `responseSchema`), and async dispatch (`start_async_task`, `check_async_task`, …) stays in PTC for `Promise.all` fan-out. No capability is lost.
- **Pinned `deepagents[quickjs]~=0.6.11`** and refreshed the lockfile, so the project develops and tests against the same versions users get.
- **Added a regression test** asserting `task` never re-enters the allowlist and that the live quickjs filter accepts the default allowlist.

---

## What's Changed

# EvoScientist v0.1.8 — Gateway Layer & Caching On by Default

G'Day! v0.1.8's headline is the new **LangGraph Gateway Layer** — a UI-agnostic abstraction that unifies how every surface (CLI, TUI, `serve`, channels) reaches the agent graph and its threads, paving the way for cleaner local/remote backends. Alongside it: **OpenRouter Anthropic prompt caching is now on by default**, so multi-turn sessions get cheaper out of the box, plus a slash-command completion fix and routine dependency upkeep.

---

### 🚪 LangGraph Gateway Layer

Graph and thread access used to be reached directly from each UI surface. v0.1.8 introduces a dedicated, UI-agnostic gateway abstraction (#295).

- **New `gateway/` package** — a `GraphGateway` protocol with `Local` and `Server` backends, so CLI, TUI, `serve`, and channel surfaces all route graph/thread access through one interface instead of touching the in-process graph directly.
- **Cleaner separation** — UI code no longer depends on how the graph is hosted, which is the groundwork for a future server/remote backend.
- **Behaviour notes** — startup session restore now covers all non-evomemory threads (previously main-agent only), and CLI thread listing gained a `graph_id` filter clause. The current runtime still wires the **local** backend, so day-to-day behaviour is unchanged.

---

### ⚡ Prompt Caching On by Default

OpenRouter Anthropic prompt caching graduated from opt-in to opt-out (#299).

- **Default flipped** — `openrouter_anthropic_prompt_cache` now defaults to **`True`**. OpenRouter + `anthropic/*` models automatically reuse the cached system prefix across calls.
- **Cheaper multi-turn** — caching is a net win for any session that reuses the system prefix within the 5-minute TTL (≈1.25× write on the first call, ≈0.1× read after), which an agent loop hits almost immediately.
- **Opting out** — set `openrouter_anthropic_prompt_cache=false` in config, or `EVOSCIENTIST_OPENROUTER_ANTHROPIC_PROMPT_CACHE=false` in the environment, to restore the previous behaviour.

---

### ⌨️ Slash-Command Completion Fix

A focused CLI input fix (#300, fixes #293).

- **Enter submits the right command** — when one command name is a prefix of another, pressing Enter now submits the intended slash command instead of the longer match.

# EvoScientist v0.1.7 — Memory Recall, Smarter Completions & Windows Resilience

G'Day! v0.1.7's headline is **Memory Retrieval** — agents can now actively *look up* their own past observations instead of only writing them. Two new read-only tools (`search_observations` + `read_memory`) make observation lookup a first-class step in every workflow, run as a per-task preflight. Rounding it out: **multi-stage slash-command completions** with subcommand awareness in both the CLI and TUI, and a batch of **Windows + interrupt-recovery fixes**. Big thanks to @din0s (memory retrieval + Windows/recovery) and @NkAntony777 (completions + path quoting)!

---

### 🧠 Memory Retrieval

Observation memory used to be write-only from the agent's side — it could `record_observation`, but had no way to query what it had recorded. v0.1.7 makes retrieval first-class (#281).

- **Two new tools** — `search_observations` (ranked keyword search) and `read_memory` (fetch a memory file by id), alongside the existing `record_observation`. Read-only tools are exposed whenever observation memory is enabled, **even when writes are disabled**.
- **Rich search** — ranked keyword search with IDF weighting (id > summary > body > metadata), regex queries, scope/type filters, result snippets, and a low-confidence fallback so a near-miss query still returns candidates.
- **Per-task preflight** — for coding, debugging, research, planning, or evaluation tasks, the agent first searches prior observations with a few distinctive keywords before diving in, so hard-won lessons resurface instead of being re-learned.
- **Reachable from `code_interpreter`** — `search_observations` and `read_memory` are on the PTC allowlist, so batched/programmatic memory lookups work too.
- **Guidance consolidated** — memory instructions now live in `EvoMemoryMiddleware` instead of being scattered across the base prompt, `think_tool`, and subagent YAML — one source of truth.

---

### 🗂️ Memory Worker Refinements

The background memory workers (profile/observation distillers) got more flexible (#281).

- **Turn workers honour `worker` / `all`** — `memory_observation_writer=worker` (or `all`) now applies to turn workers, not just subagent workers.
- **Observation-only turns** — turn workers can run observation-only when profile memory is disabled.
- **Better trajectories** — turn-worker trajectories now include direct tool results (e.g. `execute` / `code_interpreter`) while still omitting delegated subagent result bodies.
- **Clean one-shot exit** — single-shot CLI runs (`-p "…"`) now wait briefly for in-flight background memory workers before the process exits, so post-run observations aren't lost to a premature shutdown.

---

### ⌨️ Multi-Stage Slash-Command Completions

Slash-command completion is now subcommand-aware across both UIs (#273, Phase 1 of #82).

- **Subcommands surface** — typing `/mcp` now lists its 6 subcommands; `/mcp lis` narrows to `list`. `/model-fallback` (6) and `/channel` (2) gained metadata too.
- **Prefix preserved** — pressing TAB on a subcommand keeps the `/mcp ` prefix instead of replacing the whole line, with precise insertion ranges.
- **Shared engine** — the Rich CLI and Textual TUI now drive completions through one `_completion_engine`, and `/help` lists available subcommands.

---

### 🪟 Windows & Interrupt Resilience

A focused round of cross-platform and recovery fixes (#290, closes #283).

- **Windows async MCP** — async subprocess handling now installs a Proactor-based event-loop policy (`_winloop`) so MCP tool execution works on Windows.
- **Command resolution** — MCP command lookup uses an `os.access` check that behaves correctly on Windows.
- **Non-blocking workspace lookups** — workspace-directory resolution is moved off the async execution path so it can't block the event loop (langgraph dev's `blockbuster`).
- **Interrupt-safe recovery** — after a failed/crashed run the interrupted graph state is cleared, with smarter detection of paused states so the agent doesn't replay a stuck step.
- **Windows `cmd.exe` quoting** — virtual `/skills/...` mount paths are now quoted via a platform dispatcher (`_platform_quote`): POSIX keeps `shlex.quote`, Windows uses cmd.exe-compatible double-quote wrapping so literal quote chars no longer leak into argv (#280).

---

### 🐛 Fixes & Chores

- **Quoted whitespace paths** — `convert_virtual_paths_in_command` now uses a shell-aware tokenizer (`shlex`) instead of a non-quote-aware regex, so virtual paths with spaces — e.g. `python "/skills/my skill/main.py"` — are rewritten whole as a single argument instead of being truncated or left broken (#269, closes #237).
- **deepagents 0.6.10** — bumped `deepagents[quickjs]` 0.6.8 → 0.6.10 and `langchain-quickjs` → 0.2.0 (zero code changes; the only break was an unused removed export).
- **pyjwt 2.13.0 (security)** — bumped `pyjwt` 2.12.1 → 2.13.0, a security release fixing five advisories (incl. JWK-as-HMAC-secret algorithm confusion and algorithm allow-list bypass) (#289).

# EvoScientist v0.1.6 — Sessions That Survive Restarts

G'Day! v0.1.6 is a focused release with one mission: **your sessions no longer vanish when EvoScientist restarts**. The langgraph dev server (behind the WebUI and `EvoSci deploy`) now persists threads to SQLite instead of memory, and as a bonus the CLI and WebUI finally **share sessions both ways** — start a chat in the terminal, continue it in the browser, and vice versa. Thanks to @IAllenzhou for the diagnosis and the SQLite checkpointer approach that kicked this off (#277, #278)!

---

### 💾 Session Persistence for langgraph dev

WebUI and `EvoSci deploy` threads used to live in an in-memory checkpointer — one restart and they were gone (#277). They now persist in the same global SQLite `sessions.db` the CLI uses (#279).

- **SQLite checkpointer** — langgraph dev's `InMemorySaver` is replaced by the `PruningCheckpointer` on `~/.evoscientist/sessions.db`, so checkpoints survive restarts and participate in the same pruning policy as CLI threads.
- **Startup restore** — on server start, saved threads are re-injected into the API store, so the WebUI sidebar comes back exactly as you left it.
- **Scoped by design** — only main-agent threads belonging to the **current workspace** are restored. `sessions.db` is machine-global, so an unscoped restore would have exposed every workspace's history over the unauthenticated API / `--tunnel`.

---

### 🔄 CLI ⇄ WebUI Session Interop

The two surfaces now see each other's sessions — both directions.

- **WebUI → CLI** — langgraph-dev threads are stamped with `agent_name` / `workspace_dir` / `updated_at`, so WebUI sessions surface in `/threads`, `/resume`, and `/delete` alongside CLI ones.
- **CLI → WebUI** — `generate_thread_id()` now returns a full UUID, so new CLI/TUI sessions appear in the WebUI sidebar of the same workspace. Legacy 8-char-hex threads keep working in the CLI (CLI-only).
- **Real titles** — restored sidebar entries derive `metadata.title` from the first human message — no more "Untitled Thread".

---

### ✂️ Short Thread IDs

Thread ids now display as **git-style 8-char prefixes** everywhere — `/threads`, the TUI session selector, resume hints, and banners — instead of full UUIDs. Prefix matching for `/resume <id>` and `/delete <id>` is unchanged; ambiguous prefixes still fall back to a candidate list.

---

### 🧹 No More Worker Residue

Memory-worker runs (the background profile/observation distillers) used to leave checkpoint rows behind in the sessions DB.

- **Delete-on-completion** — worker threads are deleted as soon as their run finishes, in the correct accounting order.
- **Startup purge** — leftover worker checkpoints from crashed or interrupted runs are swept on server start.
- **Ghost reconciliation** — stale registry entries whose checkpoints no longer exist are dropped instead of resurrected.

---

### 📋 Upgrade Notes

- **Pre-existing WebUI sessions** (legacy `.langgraph_api/*.pckl` pickle storage) are **not carried over** — the sidebar entries are reconciled away; the pickle files remain on disk untouched. A one-time pckl→SQLite migration is planned as a follow-up.
- **Pre-existing CLI/TUI sessions are unaffected.**
- Driving the same thread from CLI and WebUI **simultaneously** won't corrupt anything (WAL serializes writes) but interleaves turns — use one surface at a time per thread.

---

### 🐛 Fixes & Chores

- **Restore metadata aggregation** — interop threads mix CLI rows (no `assistant_id`/`graph_id`) with WebUI rows; all restore metadata columns are now MAX-aggregated so SQLite can't pick an arbitrary row's NULL under `GROUP BY`.
- **`assistant_id` stays `str`** — matching the langgraph-api runtime convention (a `uuid.UUID` silently broke assistant_id-filtered searches).
- **Version** — bumped to v0.1.6.

---


## What's Changed
* fix: session lost after evoscientist restart (supersedes #278) in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/279


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/compare/v0.1.5...v0.1.6

# EvoScientist v0.1.5 — Dangerous Mode, Streaming v3 & Public Tunnels

G'Day! v0.1.5 is a power-and-polish release. The headline is **Dangerous Mode** — opt-in real-filesystem access with layered safety checks for when the sandbox is too tight — paired with a fully **rebuilt streaming pipeline** on LangGraph's v3 event protocol. Rounding it out: a **public Cloudflare tunnel** for `EvoSci deploy` (reach your agent from your phone), opt-in **Anthropic prompt caching over OpenRouter**, the new **claude-fable-5** model, a **free-scrolling TUI**, and first-class **Windows CI**.

---

### ⚠️ Dangerous Mode

A new opt-in mode that lets the agent read and write **outside** the workspace sandbox — your real filesystem — for tasks that genuinely need it, without throwing away every guardrail (#276).

- **Layered safety** — path/command validation stays on; the mode widens the reachable filesystem rather than disabling checks wholesale.
- **Loud and obvious** — a red `⚠ DANGEROUS MODE` banner is shown on startup (CLI, serve, and `EvoSci deploy`) so it's never silently on.
- **Off by default** — gated behind `dangerous_mode`; you have to deliberately turn it on.

---

### 📡 LangGraph Streaming v3

The CLI streaming pipeline was rebuilt on LangGraph's **v3 stream events** (`astream_events(version="v3")`) for cleaner, more accurate live output (#268).

- **Authoritative sub-agent identity** — sub-agents are now keyed by `instance_id` (namespace path) via the native `stream.subagents` projection, replacing the old multi-level name-resolution chain.
- **Dual-producer queue** — a single ordered drain loop merges the bare protocol stream with the sub-agent projection, so a sub-agent's tool calls never render before its start event.
- **Simpler internals** — the legacy incremental-JSON `ToolCallTracker` is gone; tool-call args now arrive complete from v3 protocol blocks.

---

### 🌐 Public Cloudflare Tunnel for `EvoSci deploy`

`EvoSci deploy --tunnel` now exposes the deploy server over a **free Cloudflare quick-tunnel**, so you can drive your own machine's agent from a phone or any remote device — no public IP, port-forwarding, or account required.

- **Zero-config** — passes `langgraph dev --tunnel`; the random `https://<name>.trycloudflare.com` URL is scraped from the log and surfaced in the Ready banner's `Public URL:` line.
- **Self-host first** — the tunnel has no auth, so a prominent `⚠ PUBLIC TUNNEL` warning reminds you to share the link only with people you trust; intended for trusted/self-hosted use (e.g. mobile access to your own box).
- **Clean lifecycle** — the tunnel lives and dies with the server; Ctrl+C tears it down and the URL is fresh on every restart.

---

### ⚡ Opt-in Anthropic Prompt Caching via OpenRouter

A new `openrouter_anthropic_prompt_cache` flag (default off) enables Anthropic prompt caching for `anthropic/*` models routed through OpenRouter (#272).

- **How** — injects a top-level `cache_control: {ephemeral}` breakpoint, which OpenRouter reads as official auto-caching (DeepAgents' built-in `AnthropicPromptCachingMiddleware` only reaches native `ChatAnthropic`, not OpenRouter).
- **When it wins** — net savings for multi-turn / long sessions (break-even at the 2nd call: 1.25× write + 0.1× read against the shared system prefix); a net loss only for genuinely isolated one-shot calls.
- **Opt-in** — off by default, so nothing changes until you enable it.

---

### 🖱️ Free-Scrolling TUI

The Textual TUI now supports **free scrolling** through the conversation, so you can scroll back through history while the agent is still streaming instead of being pinned to the bottom (#262).

---

### ✨ Models & Internals

- **claude-fable-5** — added support for the new `claude-fable-5` model.
- **Pure `create_cli_agent`** — refactored `create_cli_agent(config=, chat_model=)` to be side-effect-free, fixing a by-reference config bug where a workspace-changing `/resume` after `/model` could silently revert the model (#267).
- **`--no-reload`** — `start_langgraph_dev` now passes `--no-reload`, so editing source no longer kills in-flight async sub-agent / memory-worker tasks.

---

### 🪟 Windows & Robustness

- **Windows CI** — added `windows-latest` to the test matrix and fixed 11 cross-platform test bugs (#271).
- **Log rotation** — `langgraph_dev.log` now rotates when it grows past 50 MB, so long-running servers don't accumulate an unbounded log (#270).

---

### 🐛 Fixes & Chores

- **Tests** — hardened npx mocking (`_check_npx` / `_ensure_npx`) so headless / slow Windows runners don't trip extra onboarding prompts.
- **Docs** — README updated for the Desktop WebUI changes + demo video.
- **Version** — bumped to v0.1.5.

# EvoScientist v0.1.4 — Co-Pilot Auxiliary Model & Self-Evolving Observation Memory

G'Day! v0.1.4 is an efficiency-and-memory release. The headline is a **co-pilot "auxiliary" model** — a second, cheaper/faster model that quietly handles the background work (memory workers + tool selection) while your main agent stays on its best model — paired with an **observation-memory lifecycle** that distills reusable lessons and execution summaries from every turn. Rounding it out: a fix for **OpenRouter multi-turn reasoning** (no more `Item with id 'rs_…' not found` on the second turn), new **Qwen3.7-Max/Plus** entries, a **UI-backend selection** step in onboarding, and freshly curated **science skills**.

---

### 🤝 Co-Pilot Auxiliary Model

A new optional **auxiliary model** lets you route background/helper LLM calls to a cheaper, faster model without changing the model your main agent reasons with.

- **Two new config fields** — `auxiliary_model` + `auxiliary_provider` (both empty = transparently fall back to your main model/provider, so nothing changes until you opt in).
- **What it drives** — the **memory workers** (turn + sub-agent) and the **main agent's tool selector** run on the co-pilot model; the main orchestrator and real sub-agent work stay on your primary model, and context-editing keeps sizing against the main history.
- **One-switch onboarding** — a switch-style wizard step ("enable co-pilot?") that, when accepted, reuses the normal provider + model pickers and persists to config; both the CLI agent and the langgraph-dev memory-worker subprocess pick it up automatically.

---

### 🧠 Self-Evolving Observation Memory

Building on v0.1.3's profile-file memory, background **memory workers** now distill knowledge after each run (#259).

- **Two worker roles** — a turn-worker folds the orchestrator's turn into the **profile**, while a sub-agent-worker turns any sub-agent run into a reusable **observation** (semantic / procedural / episodic) plus an **execution summary**.
- **Fire-and-forget** — workers launch in the langgraph-dev subprocess after the agent finishes, so they never block your turn; observations are content-hash de-duped and gated by the memory controls.
- **Compounding context** — the result is memory that grows and refines itself across sessions instead of just persisting statically.

---

### 🔄 OpenRouter Multi-Turn Reasoning Fix

Reasoning models on OpenRouter (e.g. `gpt-5.5`) no longer break on the second turn.

- **Root cause** — OpenAI-Responses emits an encrypted reasoning item (`rs_*` id); OpenRouter's `/responses` beta is stateless (`store=false`), so replaying it on passback failed with `Item with id 'rs_…' not found` (seen on both Azure and OpenAI upstreams).
- **Fix** — encrypted `rs_` reasoning items are now stripped from outgoing messages on passback (exactly as the upstream error instructs), and `summary: "auto"` is enabled so a readable reasoning summary still surfaces. Reasoning display is unaffected. Refs langchain-ai/langchain#37777.

---

### ✨ Models, Onboarding & Skills

- **New models** — Qwen3.7-Max and Qwen3.7-Plus (DashScope), with context-window metadata.
- **UI-backend selection** — clearer onboarding options/descriptions for picking WebUI / TUI / CLI.
- **Curated skills** — Google DeepMind **Science Skills** (37 genomics, structural-biology & literature skills) added to the recommended packs, plus an updated K-Dense scientific-skills source.

---

### 🐛 Fixes & Chores

- **Sandbox** — fixed ssh remote path handling (#242).
- **Middleware** — repositioned the code-interpreter middleware in the stack.
- **Deps** — bumped `aiohttp` 3.13.5 → 3.14.0 (#260) and `starlette` 1.0.0 → 1.0.1 (#261).
- **Docs** — added ResearchClawBench ranking news (#257).

# EvoScientist v0.1.3 — Profile-File Memory, Runtime-Context Middleware & Multimodal Across Providers

G'Day! v0.1.3 is a memory-and-context release. The headline is a **profile-file memory system** that retires the single `MEMORY.md` blob in favour of four focused, workspace-aware profile surfaces, paired with a **runtime-context middleware** that keeps every model call grounded in live context instead of stale prompt boilerplate. On top of that, **multimodal handling now works across OpenAI-compatible and routed providers** — images and PDF/doc attachments flow through correctly, with a graceful fallback for text-only models — and a small **textual pin** restores CJK/IME input on iTerm2.

---

### 🧠 Profile-File Memory

The legacy `/memories/MEMORY.md` middleware is replaced by structured profile files under `/memories/profile/` (#253).

- **Four profile surfaces** — `SOUL.md` (agent behaviour & boundaries), `USER_PROFILE.md` (user facts, preferences, collaboration style), `RESEARCH_TASTE.md` (research interests, standards, methods to avoid), and per-workspace `projects/{project_id}/PROJECT_PROFILE.md` (conventions, commands, tests, pitfalls).
- **Workspace-aware** — project profiles are keyed from the active workspace identity (preferring git metadata), so EvoScientist keeps separate notes per repo/workspace while still sharing the global memory directory.
- **Automatic migration** — the middleware bootstraps the files, injects profile contents (or pointers) into each model call, and migrates existing `MEMORY.md` content, skipping placeholder values like `(unknown)` and preserving unmapped sections.
- **Stream timeline narration** — the streaming display was reworked into a cleaner timeline-style narration of agent activity.

---

### 🧭 Runtime-Context Middleware

A new middleware injects **live runtime context** (current date, workspace, environment) into every model call, replacing ~60 lines of static prompt boilerplate (#255).

- Keeps the agent's sense of "now" and "where" fresh on each turn instead of baking it into a fixed system prompt.
- The **research sub-agent** was updated to consume this dynamic context, trimming duplicated instructions out of `prompts.py`.

---

### 🖼️ Multimodal Across Providers

Image and document handling was reworked so attachments behave consistently on OpenAI-compatible and routed providers, not just on native Anthropic/Claude (#256).

- **Images + PDF/doc** content is flattened and hoisted correctly so strict OpenAI-compatible APIs (which require `tool` messages to be plain strings) accept media-bearing conversations.
- **Graceful fallback for text-only models** — when a model rejects media, the call is retried with an `[attachment omitted]` placeholder and the choice is cached, so the conversation continues instead of erroring out.

---

### 🐛 Fixes & Chores

- **CJK input fix** — `textual` is pinned to `>=8.0,<8.2.7`; 8.2.7's Kitty "report-all-keys" mode breaks Chinese / IME input on iTerm2 (b562343).

---

## What's Changed

* [codex] add runtime context middleware by @din0s in https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoScientist/pull/255

# EvoScientist v0.1.2 — Browser WebUI Mode, Standalone Deploy Server, Background Execution & Sonnet 4.6 Default

G'Day! v0.1.2 opens a new browser surface for EvoScientist and hardens the runtime underneath it. The headline is **WebUI mode (beta)** — one terminal now launches a deploy-style LangGraph server *and* the published `@evoscientist/webui` front-end, built on the new **`EvoSci deploy`** standalone server. We also ship **background process management** so long shell jobs survive past the 300s sandbox wall, **async completion notifications that route back to the channel that started the conversation**, the **default model bumped to `claude-sonnet-4-6`** (plus MiniMax M3 with a 1M context window), a **deepagents 0.6.7 + langchain 1.3** upgrade, and a fully **modular onboarding wizard** with scan-to-create QR onboarding for Feishu.

---

### 🖥️ Browser WebUI Mode (beta)

A third UI backend joins `tui` and `cli`. Set `ui_backend = webui` (onboard → "Select UI mode", or `EvoSci --ui webui`) and a fresh interactive session becomes, in **one terminal**, the equivalent of `EvoSci deploy` + `npx @evoscientist/webui` — no second shell to babysit (#252).

- **Always-fresh front-end** — `npx @evoscientist/webui@latest` pulls the newest published UI on every launch, so front-end fixes ship without touching your EvoScientist install.
- **Opens at `http://localhost:4716`** (`6174` reversed); change it with `EvoSci config set webui_port <port>`. Requires Node.js 24 LTS for `npx`.
- **Fresh-session only** — `-p` (one-shot) and `--resume` have concrete terminal output to render, so they fall back to the Rich CLI. Beta: the WebUI doesn't show your CLI/TUI chat history.

---

### 🚀 `EvoSci deploy` — Standalone LangGraph Server

A new subcommand serves the main agent over HTTP for external LangChain UIs and SDK clients — **no TUI, CLI agent, channel runtime, or session DB** (#228).

```bash
EvoSci deploy                   # full MCP + async sub-agents over HTTP
EvoSci deploy --port 7000       # override the langgraph dev port
```

- Built for **deep-agents-ui, agent-chat-ui, LangSmith Studio**, and `langgraph_sdk` clients.
- A **workspace fingerprint sidecar** lets independent processes safely reuse a running `langgraph dev` only when the workspace matches; stale handles are detected and cleaned.

---

### 🧰 Background Process Management + Configurable Sandbox Timeout

Long-running shell jobs used to die at the hard 300s sandbox limit. v0.1.2 makes the timeout configurable and adds first-class background execution (#243).

- The agent can launch a command in the **background** and keep working, then receive a **completion notification** when it finishes.
- Notifications are **thread-scoped, deduplicated, and HITL-aware**, and wait for the real process-finish timestamp rather than firing early.

---

### 🔔 Async Notifications Route Back to the Channel

Resolves the biggest follow-up from v0.1.0's auto-notifier (#244). When a **channel** message (iMessage, Telegram, …) spawned async sub-agents, the *later* completion turn previously rendered only to the local CLI/TUI — the phone user saw nothing.

- A per-thread **channel-origin registry** now lets all three notifier paths (Rich CLI / TUI / serve) publish the final response back to the originating channel via the message bus.
- Publish is **fire-and-forget**, so the notifier turn never blocks the event loop, and the registry is cleared on `/new` and `/resume`.

---

### 🧠 Models & 🧩 Dependencies

- **Default model** bumped from `claude-sonnet-4-5` to **`claude-sonnet-4-6`** across settings, onboarding, and the registry.
- **MiniMax M3** added with a **1M-token context window** (M2.x variants stay at the provider default).
- **deepagents 0.6.7 + langchain 1.3** upgrade, with a more robust `/resume` reconstruction path on the newer DeltaChannel storage (#251).

---

### 🪄 Onboarding — Modular Rewrite + Feishu QR
